content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 8-10. Supplemental: SEI architecture evaluation material. This unit focuses on scenarios as architectural test cases.

A scenario turns a vague quality into a testable architectural concern. Instead of saying the system must be fast, a scenario names the stimulus, source, environment, artifact, response, and response measure.
Scenarios are powerful because they connect stakeholders to evidence. They make architecture evaluation practical by asking what the system must do under specific conditions.
Studio: rewrite three vague requirements as quality attribute scenarios with measurable response criteria.

concepts.name: Quality attribute scenario
concepts.description: A structured statement that makes a quality concern testable through stimulus, environment, response, and response measure.

concepts.name: Stimulus
concepts.description: The event or condition that triggers a system response in a scenario.

concepts.name: Response measure
concepts.description: The observable criterion used to judge whether a scenario response is acceptable.

concepts.name: Scenario prioritization
concepts.description: The process of ranking scenarios by stakeholder importance, risk, cost, and architectural impact.
